title: Properties of the final finite-presentation envelope
statement:
The map $i_f^{\mathrm{fp}}\colon X\hookrightarrow X_f^{\mathrm{fp}}$ is a
closed immersion over $S$, and
$X_f^{\mathrm{fp}}\to S$ is separated and of finite presentation.

proof.text: Work with the hypotheses inherited through [def-nagata-final-fp-envelope] from [def-nagata-finite-type-closed-in-fp]: $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to S$ is separated and of finite type. By the final-envelope definition, $(X_f^{\mathrm{fp}},i_f^{\mathrm{fp}})=\mathsf{Env}_{\mathrm{fp}}(X/S)=(X^{\mathrm{fp}},i^{\mathrm{fp}}_{X/S})$. Taking the two components identifies $X_f^{\mathrm{fp}}=X^{\mathrm{fp}}$ and $i_f^{\mathrm{fp}}=i^{\mathrm{fp}}_{X/S}$; their structure maps to $S$ are the same structure map of the selected model. This is an equality of the defined objects, not a comparison with a different existence witness.

source.place: Proof, interpreted using def-nagata-final-fp-envelope (order 399) and def-nagata-finite-type-closed-in-fp (order 396)

proof.text: Apply [prop-nagata-finite-type-closed-in-fp] to this explicit envelope under exactly the hypotheses of step 1. Its statement says that $X^{\mathrm{fp}}\to S$ is separated and of finite presentation and that $i^{\mathrm{fp}}_{X/S}:X\to X^{\mathrm{fp}}$ is a closed immersion over $S$. Substitute the component equalities from step 1. The closed-immersion clause becomes the assertion for $i_f^{\mathrm{fp}}$, and the other two clauses become separatedness and finite presentation of $X_f^{\mathrm{fp}}\to S$. The words over $S$ include the equality of the composite with $f$, so the asserted closed immersion is over the original base.
